facts.name: Program aim
facts.detail: The M.S. is described as deepening hardware and software themes and stressing technical competence and independent work.
facts.quote: The Master of Science program in Computer Science provides an opportunity for students to enhance their understanding of the principal hardware and software themes.

facts.name: Evening classes
facts.detail: The FAQ says the program offers evening classes across a wide range of computer science topics.
facts.quote: Evening classes with a wide range of topics in computer science

facts.name: Department also plans an online M.S.
facts.detail: The department home page announces an Online Master of Science in Computer Science coming up in Fall 2026; that is a different program from this on-campus M.S.
facts.quote: Online Master of Science in Computer Science

facts.name: Undergraduate CS presumption
facts.detail: Admission presumes an undergraduate computer science degree or equivalent core coursework; students without that preparation cannot be admitted.
facts.quote: The graduate program is based on the presumption that the student has an undergraduate degree with a major in computer science, or equivalent coursework in the principal computer science and mathematics subjects required

facts.name: Admission is competitive
facts.detail: Meeting minimum requirements does not guarantee admission.
facts.quote: These are minimum requirements for the program admission. Admission is competitive and meeting minimum requirement does not guarantee admission to the program.

facts.name: Unconditional GPA
facts.detail: Unconditional admission requires a bachelor's in CS or a closely related field with a GPA of 3.0 or better in all courses or in the most recent 60 semester units.
facts.quote: Applicants seeking unconditional admission must have a bachelor's degree in Computer Science or closely related field with a GPA of 3.0 or better in all courses or the most recent 60 semester units attempted

facts.name: Unconditional topic coverage
facts.detail: Required background includes calculus, probability and statistics, object-oriented programming, discrete structures, data structures, computer organization, algorithms, computer architecture, operating systems, and software engineering.
facts.quote: 10-12 semester units including Calculus and Probability and Statistics

facts.name: Conditional admission
facts.detail: Applicants with a bachelor's degree and a GPA above 3.0 who do not meet unconditional requirements may seek conditional admission, with priority given to unconditional admissions first.
facts.quote: Applicants who do not meet unconditional admission but have a bachelor's degree with a GPA above 3.0 may seek conditional admission. However, priority will be given to unconditional admissions first.

facts.name: International students not conditionally admitted
facts.detail: International students who need an I-20 will not be conditionally admitted and must meet all requirements before admission.
facts.quote: However, per CSU Admissions and SEVIS Policy, international students attending the University on a visa requiring issuance of an I-20 will NOT be conditionally admitted and must meet all requirements prior to gaining admission to the University.

facts.name: Conditional students and aid
facts.detail: Students in conditional standing do not qualify for federal financial aid until they are in unconditional standing.
facts.quote: Students in conditional standing do not qualify for federal financial aid until they are in unconditional standing.

facts.name: English language requirement
facts.detail: Applicants whose native language is not English and whose bachelor's instruction was not in English must meet IELTS 6.5 or TOEFL 213 computer / 550 paper / 80 internet.
facts.quote: must have passed the International English Language Testing System (IELTS) exam with a minimum score of 6.5 or the Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) exam with a minimum score of 213 on the computer-based, or 550 on the paper-based, or 80 on the Internet-based TOEFL.

facts.name: Supplemental application form
facts.detail: A program supplemental form is required and applications missing it may be declined without review.
facts.quote: This Program Application form is REQUIRED and applications missing this completed form uploaded to Cal State Mentor site may be declined without review.

facts.name: SOP, resume, letters, unofficial transcript
facts.detail: Applicants must also submit a statement of purpose, resume/CV, two letters of recommendation, and an unofficial PDF transcript on Cal State Apply.
facts.quote: applicants are REQUIRED to submit a statement of purpose (why applying to CPP CS MS program and how it will help to achieve your career objectives), resume/CV, two letters of recommendation and unoffical pdf transcript on Cal State Apply.

facts.name: GRE not required
facts.detail: The department does not require the GRE, but recommends it if the major GPA does not meet 3.0.
facts.quote: The department does not require the GRE. However, it is recommended that you take it if your major GPA does not meet the 3.0 requirement.

facts.name: GPA to maintain
facts.detail: A 3.0 GPA or better must be maintained in all upper-division undergraduate and all graduate courses.
facts.quote: A grade point average of 3.0 (B) or better must be maintained in all upper-division undergraduate and all graduate courses.

facts.name: Transfer unit cap
facts.detail: No more than 9 semester units of acceptable graduate credit may be transferred from another graduate institution.
facts.quote: No more than 9 semester units of acceptable graduate credit may be transferred from another graduate institution.

facts.name: Combined transfer limit
facts.detail: A total limit of 9 semester units of transfer, Extended University, and/or petitioned units may be included on a master's contract, with a 7-year time limit.
facts.quote: A total limit of 9 semester units of transfer, Extended University, and/or units petitioned for graduate credit may be included on a master's contract. The stipulated time limit of 7 years applies to all of the above.

facts.name: Total units
facts.detail: The program requires 30 units in total.
facts.quote: TOTAL UNITS REQUIRED: 30 units

facts.quote: CS 5250 Advanced Computer Architecture (3 units)

facts.quote: CS 5300 Advanced Algorithm Design and Analysis (3units)

facts.name: CS 5800

facts.quote: CS 5800 Advanced Software Engineering (3 units)

facts.quote: CS 6640 Graduate Seminar (1 unit)

facts.quote: CS 6910 Directed Study (1 unit) and

facts.name: Thesis option units

facts.name: Elective units
facts.detail: Students select 18 elective units with the project option or 15 elective units with the thesis option.
facts.quote: Select 18 units (with Master's Degree Project) or 15 units (with Master's Degree Thesis) from the following list of courses or other courses approved by the Computer Science Graduate Committee:

facts.name: 4000-level electives
facts.detail: M.S. students may use up to 6 semester units of CS 4000-level electives, with listed exclusions, and may not repeat undergraduate classes already taken.
facts.quote: Computer Science MS students can take up to 6 semester units of CS 4000+ levels elective classes to satisfy their elective courses requirement, excluding the following courses: CS 4000, CS 4310, CS 4610, CS 4620, CS 4630, and CS 4800.

facts.name: Required courses offered yearly
facts.detail: Required courses CS 5250, CS 5300, CS 5800, and CS 6640 are offered every year; other CS 5xxx courses every two years.
facts.quote: The required courses CS 5250, CS 5300, CS 5800 and CS 6640 are offered every year. All other graduate courses CS 5xxx are offered every two years.

facts.name: Evening graduate courses
facts.detail: Graduate courses traditionally meet in late afternoons and evenings.
facts.quote: Graduate courses traditionally meet in late afternoons and evenings.
